title: Single-tape simulation of all inputs
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite, decidable alphabet, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with a positive number $k$ of work tapes, and choose a default symbol $a_0\in\Gamma$. Suppose that $M$ computes a function $f$ on every input in time $T$ of the input length, and that for every input word $y$ and every time $t$, the space used by $M$ on $y$ through time $t$ is at most $S(|y|)$. Then the single-tape simulator associated with $M$ and $a_0$ computes, on each encoded input $x$, the encoding of $f$ applied to the word obtained by replacing each symbol of $x$ by its image under the retraction that sends internal simulator symbols to $a_0$, within $(9k+6)(T(|x|)+1)^2$ steps; at every time $t$, its space use is at most $(9k+6)(S(|x|)+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: $\Gamma$ is finite and has decidable equality.
$M$ is a finite Turing machine and $0<k$, where $k$ is its number of work tapes.
$f$ maps words over $\Gamma$ to words over $\Gamma$; $T,S$ map natural numbers to natural numbers.
For every input, $M$ computes $f$ in time $T$ of its length.
For every word $y$ and every time $t$, the space used by $M$ on $y$ through time $t$ is at most $S(|y|)$.
An input word $x$ over the enlarged simulator alphabet is given.
